transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because I keep making these little mistakes that are starting to bother me. Like I’ll write the wrong time down on a senior-center class sheet, or I’ll measure a board and still cut it just a bit short because I skipped over some small print. It’s not huge things, but it keeps happening.
Have you been having any trouble with your eyesight?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything obvious with my eyesight, but I haven’t really thought about it much.
Have you been having any difficulty reading small print?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed small print being a problem, at least not in a way that stood out to me.
When you look at writing on a page, do the words or numbers ever look blurry?
I can’t say I’ve really noticed them looking blurry. If they are, it hasn’t been obvious to me.
Do you ever miss things that are off to one side when you’re looking at a page or object?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed missing things off to the side when I’m looking at something.
Have you been feeling unusually worried or nervous lately?
Not especially, no. I mean, I get concerned about things now and then like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually worried or nervous lately.
Have you been forgetting recent conversations or appointments?

Sometimes, yeah. It’s not always that I forget the whole conversation, but I don’t take in what was said. Like my wife will be looking right at me and say something like, “Dave, the cards are in the hall closet now,” and then a minute later I realize I heard her talking but I don’t know where she said they were.
Have you had any trouble hearing what people say?
I don’t think I have trouble hearing, no. It’s more like I hear that someone’s talking, but sometimes I don’t really catch it unless I’m paying attention.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on what someone is saying?

Yes, sometimes. Like I said, my wife can be looking right at me telling me something simple, like, “Dave, the cards are in the hall closet now,” and a minute later I realize I heard her talking, but I didn’t really take in where she said they were.
If you make a point to pay close attention when someone tells you something, are you usually able to remember it afterward?

If I really make myself pay attention, I do better, yes. It’s more when I’m not locked in on it. My wife can tell me something plain, like where she moved the cards, and I hear her voice, but a minute later I don’t know where she said they were.
When was your last eye exam?
I’m not sure, honestly. It’s been a while, but I don’t remember exactly when.
Do you ever look right at words or numbers and still have trouble recognizing what they are?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might have to look twice if I’m distracted or the print is small, but I haven’t really noticed looking straight at a word or number and not recognizing it.
Have these problems started to interfere with things like managing your bills or medications?

Not so much bills or medications, no. It’s been more with plans and things I’m supposed to help with. I’ve had enough mix-ups that I stepped back from helping lead a couple DIY workshops, and my wife usually double-checks plans now so I don’t mess up family visits or things at the center.
Do you now need help managing your finances?
No, I don’t think I need help with finances right now. I can still manage that okay.
Do you need help keeping track of your appointments?

Not usually just the appointment by itself. It’s more when I’ve got a few errands, maybe a workshop to get ready for, and an appointment all on the same day. I have trouble putting it all in order, and I’ll start one thing, stop, then end up rushing around at the end.
Because of these thinking problems, do you now need someone else to take over any of your usual day-to-day tasks?

Not take over, no. I still do my regular day-to-day things. But the mix-ups have made me step back from helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops, and my wife double-checks plans now so I don’t throw off family visits or things at the center.
Because of these thinking problems, do you need help shopping on your own?
No, I don’t need help shopping on my own. I can handle that. Maybe I take a list with me sometimes, but I’m not needing someone to go with me or do it for me.
Do these thinking problems ever make you unable to complete a task that you used to handle on your own?

Not unable exactly, but I’ve had to back off from some things I used to do. Like helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops — the mix-ups were causing problems. And my wife double-checks plans now, so I don’t mess up family visits or things going on at the center.
Do you feel these thinking problems are a clear change from how you used to function before?

Not really a clear change, no. I mean, I’ve had this kind of thing since I was a kid. Even in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books, lose homework, or just stare out the window unless someone kept me on track.
As a child, did you have the same trouble paying attention both at school and at home?

Yes, school for sure. I remember even in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books, lose homework, or just be staring out the window unless someone kept me on track. At home it was similar enough, but the school part is what I remember most clearly.
